claims.claim: Garmin provides a signed-in Export Your Data route for account holders.
claims.evidence: The official Export Your Data endpoint redirects an unauthenticated visitor to Garmin Account Management SSO.

claims.claim: The Garmin Connect Developer Program is an enterprise/business integration surface rather than unrestricted personal developer access.
claims.evidence: Garmin's FAQ says the program is available for enterprise use and is only for business use.

claims.claim: All Garmin Connect Developer Program APIs use OAuth 2.0.
claims.evidence: The program FAQ explicitly answers that all APIs in the Developer Program use OAuth 2.0.

claims.claim: The Garmin Connect Health API supplies JSON health data including heart rate, steps, calories, sleep, respiration, body composition, stress, pulse ox and epoch summaries.
claims.evidence: The official Health API page lists these data families and states that supported-device data is supplied in JSON after user consent.

claims.claim: Commercial use of the Garmin Connect Health API requires a licence fee.
claims.evidence: The official Health API page includes the explicit note: Commercial use requires a license fee payment.

claims.claim: Garmin advertises backfill user data within pre-production Developer Web Tools, not as a documented guarantee of live pre-consent historical retrieval.
claims.evidence: The Health API page places sample data, backfill user data, and auto-verification together under easy onboarding and Developer Web Tools before production.

claims.claim: The Garmin Connect Activity API can provide complete activity details as FIT, GPX or TCX files after user consent and device synchronization.
claims.evidence: The official Activity API page lists FIT, GPX and TCX files and explains that data becomes available after initial consent and Garmin Connect synchronization.

claims.claim: Garmin Health SDKs provide direct mobile and real-time wearable data access only to approved enterprise partners.
claims.evidence: Garmin describes the Standard and Companion SDKs as available to Garmin Health enterprise partners through an access request and evaluation licence.

claims.claim: Garmin FIT is a documented file protocol for storing and sharing sport, fitness and health-device data, not an account authentication API.
claims.evidence: Garmin documents FIT messages, SDKs and tools for encoding and decoding files already transferred from devices.

claims.claim: Garmin Connect can automatically synchronize activities to Strava after the accounts are connected.
claims.evidence: Strava's current Garmin article describes connecting a Garmin device or Garmin Connect account for automatic activity synchronization.

claims.claim: TrainingPeaks can receive Garmin activities and selected health data, send structured workouts to Garmin, and optionally backfill up to five years of prior workouts.
claims.evidence: TrainingPeaks documents activity/body data from Garmin, workouts to Garmin, an optional five-year prior-workout sync, and no historical daily-health backfill.

claims.claim: Garmin and MyFitnessPal exchange selected workout, step, calorie and weight records, and information from before account linking is not transferred.
claims.evidence: MyFitnessPal lists the exact categories in each direction and states that only future information posts after linking.

claims.claim: python-garminconnect provides broad personal Garmin Connect retrieval using the consumer mobile authentication flow rather than the approved Developer Program.
claims.evidence: The project documents more than 130 account methods, JSON export, Garmin mobile SSO and locally stored refresh tokens.

claims.claim: The pe-st Garmin Connect exporter is currently blocked by Garmin TLS fingerprinting and is not a dependable working route.
claims.evidence: The maintainer states that the community could not work around Garmin's new TLS fingerprinting and probably will not continue until access is possible.
